comment_text:
While I am not an admirer of Apple, I must acknowledge—after purchasing the Samsung Galaxy S25—that the device falls short in terms of battery performance. This shortfall is largely attributable to Samsung’s emphasis on achieving a slim form factor, which results in a reduced battery capacity. Consequently, the phone struggles to last a full day under moderate use, and the standby power drain is notably higher compared to that of the iPhone.

For context, I also use my  employer-issued iPhone 15 alongside the S25, allowing me to compare their performance in daily usage scenarios. Based on this direct comparison, I find the iPhone 15 delivers superior battery life under similar conditions. My usage includes browsing, YouTube, Instagram, GPS navigation, and regular phone calls, with no gaming involved.

Additionally, the Galaxy S25 tends to exhibit heating issues during regular use—a concern occasionally observed in the iPhone as well, no complaints there. Ultimately, my primary grievance centers on inadequate battery endurance. The trade-off between slim design and battery capacity, which often necessitates carrying an external power bank, is unsatisfactory for my needs.

I sincerely hope @Samsung takes this feedback into account in future product designs.

comment_text:
Thank you MKBHD for speaking up on behalf of Samsung users here. Samsung is indeed very comfortable with their offering these days and started to invent useless stuffs and imitating Apple a LOT. On S24 Ultra, they release this A.I drawing assist that turns your drawing cat into 'real' cat at the expense of popular GIF maker (at least temporarily, until users made a big fuss about it and they bringing it back). Seriously? If we want stupid feature like that we'll get an iPhone. The only reason why I always pick Samsung over the others simply because of its productivity softwares. Flow, Dex, Spen, SNotes, Screen cast, This is a go-to phone for productivity freak. So, instead of spending your R&D on funky A.I features and imitating iPhone, put your resources into full fledge on powerful photo / video editing software that seamlessly running on both PC and Android, make ppt slides making on-the-go easier, make SNote works seamlessly with MS Word, Excel & Powerpoint, make Samsung Calendar integration seamless with Google Cal and Outlook, this is how Samsung could remain competitive as a phone for business. They dont seemed to do much of that these days.

Apple did that innovation many years ago and lock the users into their own ecosystem. However, in one of the biggest Germany companies that i'm working for, we are already phasing out Macbook and iPhone little by little from our inventories. Supporting OSX is really not worth the money and hassles, for all we care they could live on their own rules and policies and we are going back to FOSS and open ecosystem. This is where Samsung could be the new contender as true business phone in an open ecosystem that plays well with Windows and Linux. Do not underestimated linux influence, investing into linux and FOSS probably the best decision Microsoft could have made that saves Microsoft years ago. Dont get stuck up in playing catch up and hardware race, it wont be long before Chinese phone manufacturers copied your Spen with a cheaper price and competitive software and experience. By then it will be too late to innovate. Dont think so? just take a look at the auto industry.

A: If you're worried about people being able to view your personal information when you're in a crowded space, you can activate Privacy Display to hide your full screen from others.

A: Wider apertures mean the 200 MP Wide camera opens to F1.4. The 50 MP Telephoto camera, with 5x optical zoom and 10x optical quality zoom, now opens to F2.9. This allows in more light for improved brightness.
Q: What's the new key AI feature available on Galaxy S26 Ultra?
A: Now Nudge is a new feature that intelligently understands what's on your screen and will provide suggestions, such as viewing your ‘Calendar’ to add an event or the option to jump straight to your ‘Gallery’ when someone asks you to share photos with them.
